summary: Rock: 100-140 BPM, a big acoustic kit on a straight backbeat, a picked bass on root 8ths locked to the kick, distorted guitar power chords with the bVII, an overdriven guitar lead; knowledge/style/rock.json is its template
body: Tempo 100-140 BPM, mid-tempo classic rock about 120; punk goes past 160, ballads below 90.
Drums: a live acoustic kit, big and punchy: kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, straight 8th hats or ride; tom and crash fills at phrase ends.
Bass: a picked electric bass on driving root 8ths, locked to the kick; the bass guitar, not a sub, carries the low end, with some grit.
Harmony: I-IV-V with the mixolydian bVII (I-bVII-IV); minor i-VII-VI; distorted power chords, often doubled and panned wide; keys E, A, D.
Lead: an overdriven electric guitar for riffs and solos.
Texture/master: loud, saturated and energetic; solid low mids, bus compression for glue; driven, never lofi.

Sources (2026-11-26): Violet Recording 'How to Make Rock Music'; iZotope '6 tips for mixing good ol' fashioned rock and roll'; Mastering The Mix 'How to Mix Big, Punchy Rock Drums'; Drumeo 'A Drummer's Guide to Rock'.
Apply: pattern/basic-rock on the drums, then pattern/prog-rock-characteristic-1 on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/rock.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
